baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ ءَالِهَتِي and the conditional تَنتَهِ / أَرْجُمَنَّكَ / ٱهْجُرْنِي chain.
baseline_models.mechanism: The preposition عن fixes رغبة as desire turned away. The speaker treats inward orientation as an actionable breach, demands that it reach a stop, and escalates from threatened injury or expulsion to prolonged separation.

activation_trace.role: Desire directed toward or away from an object supplies the disputed inward orientation.
The worshipped objects supply the allegiance from which Abraham is accused of turning.
Cessation under rebuke functions as the demanded endpoint of Abraham's conduct.
Cursing, driving out, and removal from good supply the threat's expulsive force.
Severance and departure make distance the enforced consequence.
Extended time gives the commanded separation duration rather than mere direction.
The alternate mapped root contributes deliberate allowance or extension of the interval.

changed_reading.before: A father simply threatens stoning and tells his son to go away.
changed_reading.after: The utterance polices allegiance: Abraham's withdrawn desire must cease, or injury, expulsion, and a deliberately extended suspension of relation will enforce the boundary.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: قَالَ, لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ, and وَٱهْجُرْنِي occur in one spoken escalation.
baseline_models.mechanism: The threat can move through speech as well as stone: رجم includes injurious words likened to thrown stones, while هجر includes both foul speech and relational severance. The line therefore lets verbal assault perform the first stage of exclusion.

activation_trace.role: Voiced utterance supplies the medium in which the threat is enacted.
Injurious speech figured as stone-throwing makes verbal attack a live sense of the threat.
Deliberately foul speech links the threat's language to the following command of estrangement.
Bodily, verbal, or affective severance turns hostile speech into social rupture.

changed_reading.before: لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ denotes only a prospective physical stoning.
changed_reading.after: The threat remains physically dangerous but also names speech used as a projectile, already beginning the exclusion completed by وَٱهْجُرْنِي.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The closing unit وَٱهْجُرْنِي مَلِيًّا joins severance to temporal extension.
baseline_models.mechanism: هجر removes contact, while both mappings of ملو emphasize duration and granted extension. The final command regulates not just where Abraham may be but how long the relationship is to remain suspended.

activation_trace.role: Separation supplies the suspended contact.
Temporal extension makes the separation an interval.
The second mapping independently reinforces length of time rather than spatial remoteness alone.

changed_reading.before: مَلِيًّا intensifies a vague command to leave.
changed_reading.after: The closing phrase imposes a managed duration of non-contact, leaving open whether the interval is respite, cooling-off period, or indefinite banishment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding father-address asks why he worships what cannot hear, see, or suffice. The reply does not answer those capacities; it recasts the dispute as Abraham's withdrawal from the father's gods, converting an argument about efficacy into a filial and cultic loyalty test.

activation_trace.role: Turning desire away supplies the substitute charge through which the earlier argument is reframed.
The possessive worshipped objects become the center of the loyalty claim.
Repeated direct address to the father makes filial relation the social channel of the dispute.
Submissive worship identifies the practice whose justification Abraham had challenged.
Auditory incapacity supplies one unanswered criterion of efficacy.
Visual incapacity supplies the paired unanswered criterion.
Failure to suffice supplies the practical criterion displaced by the father's question.

structural_cues: 19:42 places the efficacy challenge before 19:46, while 19:46 answers with a question about Abraham's رغبة rather than the gods' capacities.
The repeated يَا أَبَتِ of 19:42-45 yields in 19:46 to the father's direct vocative يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the sequence, paternal address, worship, and failed capacities; I infer that changing the subject to رغبة turns critique into a loyalty test. A live alternative is simple shock rather than a deliberate rhetorical displacement.

changed_reading.before: The father asks a direct question about Abraham's religious preference.
changed_reading.after: The question defensively relocates the issue from whether the gods can act to whether a son may withdraw allegiance from his father's gods.

context_deltas.mechanism: Abraham first warns that punishment may touch his father and that the father may become an ally of the rebellious one. The father answers with his own conditional warning of injury and separation, reversing who is dangerous, who is misaligned, and whose conduct must stop.

activation_trace.role: The demand to cease turns Abraham from warning speaker into the conduct to be restrained.
Injurious speech or attack supplies the father's counter-threat.
Severance makes exclusion the father's proposed remedy.
Departure from obedience supplies the prior diagnosis that the reply implicitly throws back at Abraham.
Anticipatory fear supplies Abraham's warning posture before the father counter-warns.
The arrival of a harmful effect supplies the threatened outcome in Abraham's warning.
Painful punishment supplies the danger Abraham fears for his father.
Alliance and support supply the relational misalignment Abraham warns against.

structural_cues: 19:45 has a feared conditional outcome for the father; 19:46 immediately returns a conditional threat against Abraham.
The threatened touch of punishment is answered by threatened رجم, and warned alliance is answered by commanded separation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent warnings, rebellion, alliance, harm, and severance; I infer a retaliatory reversal in which the father casts Abraham as the danger. The alternative is unpatterned anger with no deliberate mirroring.

changed_reading.before: The father abruptly loses patience and threatens Abraham.
changed_reading.after: The father counter-warns: he reverses Abraham's diagnosis, treats the warning itself as disobedience, and substitutes paternal violence and exclusion for the danger Abraham had feared for him.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate answer pairs peace with promised intercession and recollection of the father's care. Abraham accepts distance without returning abusive speech or relational curse, making the rupture ethically asymmetric.

activation_trace.role: Injurious speech supplies the hostile mode Abraham declines to mirror.
Severance supplies the distance that the reply accepts without matching its hostility.
Peace rather than war supplies the reply's counter-mode.
Seeking the covering of fault preserves care for the person who threatened exclusion.
Care, honor, and gentleness keep remembered relational good alive after the threat.

structural_cues: 19:47 begins سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ immediately after the threat and retains second-person concern through أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ.
The reply neither repeats the conditional threat nor commands a counter-expulsion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate peace, sought forgiveness, and remembered care; I infer that these deliberately refuse reciprocity with the threat. سلام may alternatively function as a conventional leave-taking, but the promised care keeps the asymmetry live.

changed_reading.before: وَٱهْجُرْنِي begins a mutual and complete relational break.
changed_reading.after: The father initiates enforced distance, but Abraham answers with safety and continuing concern; contact ends without reciprocal verbal violence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The father's singular command to leave him is answered by Abraham's first-person withdrawal from the whole group and what they invoke besides God. Subsequent gifts and prophetic making turn threatened deprivation into a transition that generates other relations.

activation_trace.role: Imposed separation supplies the act Abraham subsequently takes up as his own.
Extended time supplies the interval across which withdrawal becomes a new social condition.
Self-removal to a side converts commanded expulsion into deliberate withdrawal.
Calling and invocation expand the object of withdrawal from one father to a worship practice.
The worshipped object anchors the plural withdrawal to the same cultic dispute named in 19:46.
Gift without exchange supplies replacement relation after Abraham leaves.
Transformation into a prophetic state makes the aftermath productive rather than empty.

structural_cues: The imperative ٱهْجُرْنِي in 19:46 is followed by Abraham's وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ in 19:48, shifting singular object to plural and command to chosen action.
19:49-50 follow withdrawal with gifts, making, mercy, and elevated truthful mention.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the lexical sequence from imposed severance to self-withdrawal and then gifts; I infer that Abraham appropriates the expulsion as principled agency and that the gifts answer its social loss. The withdrawal may have been independently intended rather than caused by the command.

changed_reading.before: Abraham merely obeys a private order to leave his father for a long time.
changed_reading.after: He converts expulsion into chosen, plural-facing disaffiliation from a worship system, and the extended absence becomes the opening for replacement kinship and vocation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links the verbal branch of رجم to later public speech rather than reducing the threat to stones. It remains anchored because the packet explicitly gives injurious speech for رجم and later joins tongue, truth, and elevation. Render it only as a secondary reputational reversal, never as a denial of physical danger.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: قَالَ and لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ make hostile speech a possible layer of the threat.

activation_trace.role: Speech circulating among people supplies the possible reputational reach of the father's threat.
Injurious words likened to thrown stones supply the threatened hostile voice.
The tongue as speech organ supplies the later countervoice.
Truthful speech supplies the quality that reverses hostile verbal projection.
Elevation and honor give the truthful tongue enduring public standing.

changed_reading.before: The father threatens only Abraham's body.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the father also threatens Abraham with a hostile public voice, while the later elevated tongue of truth reverses that attempted reputational exclusion.

strongest_changes: The father's reply displaces Abraham's efficacy critique into a filial loyalty test centered on 'my gods.'
The threat reverses Abraham's prior warning, but Abraham's immediate peace makes the resulting separation ethically asymmetric.
Abraham converts commanded expulsion into deliberate withdrawal from a wider cultic system, followed by gifted replacement relations.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah is a hinge where desire, paternal authority, threat, speech, and duration compress into one ultimatum; the adjacent ayat then unpack its reversal and Abraham's nonreciprocal response.
remaining_uncertainties: رجم keeps physical stoning, abusive speech, cursing, and expulsion live without forcing one exclusive sense.
مَلِيًّا clearly extends the separation, but the focus alone does not decide between respite, cooling-off interval, and indefinite banishment.
The post-withdrawal gifts structurally answer loss, but a direct causal claim remains reader-supplied.
